FluvialGeomorph is local-first: its feature classes and related tables are held
in a local geodatabase, with analytical rasters stored as external GeoTIFFs. In
the open-source workflow the vector/table container is OGC GeoPackage. FGDB defines
the enduring data objects, ownership and acceptance contracts; functions create,
use and revise representations of those objects.

Read this article alongside the function-flow chapters. Their **Data objects and
storage** tables identify each operation's domain inputs, outputs and physical
representation. Exact internal revision filenames and worker files belong to
implementation schemas, rather than defining the data model.

## Stream terrain shared by Reaches

The intended application design processes a DEM at Stream scale and lets Reaches
use that same terrain asset. Reach-based analysis supplies its spatial domain and
references the applicable Stream DEM edition; a Reach boundary alone is not a
reason to rebuild, copy or permanently clip the DEM. A bounded read or temporary
crop may support an operation without becoming a duplicate terrain product.

Terrain extent, raster identity and the identity of a consuming Reach Survey Event
are separate concerns. Associations must identify the exact terrain edition and
applicable acquisition period so results remain reproducible when terrain changes.
The physical design direction is an external Stream GeoTIFF referenced by the
applicable Reach/Event records, with relationships and metadata in the local
GeoPackage/delivery binding. Exact relationship tables and keys require FGDB
schema definition; this article does not invent their physical names.

The current app implements Stream assembly, reuse and local hydro-modification.
Binding shared terrain to downstream Reach analyses is not yet integrated. The
owner's direction is to retain Stream-scale processing as these capabilities
mature. FGDB's existing Reach-Survey-Event hydro DEM ownership rule must be revised
to express that sharing; it must not force independent DEM production per Reach.
Other Reach-owned features and Survey Event relationships are not changed by this
terrain-sharing direction.

Archived legacy projects may retain only a Reach-Survey-Event hydro DEM. Preserve
that GeoTIFF at its actual extent and retain its original Event association and
provenance. It remains usable without reconstructing a Stream DEM. The storage
model therefore accommodates both new shared Stream terrain and legacy
Reach-scoped terrain: an asset's extent and identity are separate from the Reach
Events that consume it. Do not mosaic legacy rasters merely to conform to the new
processing pattern.

## Existing FGDB ownership contract

```text
FGDB Collection
  Study Area
    Stream
      Reach
        Survey Event
          governed feature datasets and raster products
```

Stable identifiers and explicit parent relationships establish ownership. Display
names, dates, filenames and spatial containment do not establish parentage.
A Survey Event belongs to one Reach. Reprocessing changes its derived content,
not its position in the hierarchy. Stream/Study summaries traverse that ownership
rather than duplicating Reach-owned products.

The Study Area has a governed polygon; Stream, Reach and Survey Event geometry
are optional in FGDB. The current terrain-processing functions require the
polygons needed for their masks. That algorithmic input requirement does not make
optional geometry mandatory throughout the FGDB model.

FGDB also governs Study-Area-owned Stream Network Configurations and time-specific
Network Observations. Reference hydrography used to choose app Stream geometry
is not automatically a governed terrain-derived network observation.

## Objects, physical structure and function responsibilities

Physical names below identify existing local representations where implemented.
They are not declarations of final enterprise feature-class names. The FGDB kernel
relational model remains a design-review draft; exact local delivery bindings are
pending where indicated.

| Object | Local physical representation | Function relationship | FGDB relationship |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Collection | No FGDB Collection binding in the app yet | Study creation does not assign enterprise Collection membership | Top-level ownership/governance partition; required for governed Study Areas |
| Study Area | GeoPackage `study_area` polygon/table and stable ID | `start_study_context()` creates; `revise_study_context()` updates; readers supply geometry and identity | Maps conceptually to Study Area; district/name, extent type, collection and enterprise spatial binding require FGDB conformance |
| Stream | GeoPackage `streams`, with Study Area parent ID and optional polygon | `define_study_streams()` or `add_study_stream_corridor()` creates; `rename_study_feature()` updates; Reach and terrain functions consume | Mandatory child entity of Study Area; selected national hydrography is provenance, not its governed ID |
| Reach | GeoPackage `reaches`, with Stream parent ID and optional polygon | `add_study_reach_corridor()`, `merge_study_reaches()`, `split_study_reach()` create/revise; downstream analysis uses Reach identity | Normative spatial owner of Survey Events and unit of derivation |
| Survey Event | GeoPackage `survey_events`, when supplied, with Reach parent ID and year/optional month/day | Context readers preserve records; app Event definitions can link existing IDs but do not create these Reach Event rows | Governs a terrain condition/acquisition period and its derived content |
| Analysis reference | GeoPackage `analysis_reference` and `vertical_reference` tables; CRS also attached to geometry/rasters | `set_study_analysis_crs()` and `set_study_vertical_reference()` record specifications; processing reads them | Supplies spatial/scientific provenance; selecting a target is not transforming a product |
| Hydro-modified DEM | External numerical GeoTIFF, associated with consuming Reach Survey Events through delivery metadata | Local Hydro Modify uses `burn_hydro_cutlines()` and saves source-linked GeoTIFF editions; governed delivery binding remains pending | Governed terrain product; existing Reach ownership requires reconciliation with shared Stream terrain |
| Other governed FG features/products | GeoPackage feature layers/attribute tables; external GeoTIFFs for raster products | Downstream producers are not integrated by the current DEM assembly | Feature catalog governs object meaning, ownership, attributes and edition acceptance |

The app's local hierarchy can be incomplete during study definition. It is not
therefore a fully qualified FGDB delivery. FGDB requires complete governed
parentage and its own spatial/attribute contract at the relevant boundary.

## Preparation assets and their relation to governed objects

Local preparation is durable when needed for reproducibility without becoming a
new FGDB domain entity. Preserve the distinction in both code and documentation.

| Preparation asset | Physical structure | Producer/consumer | Relationship to governed content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Survey Collection selection | GeoPackage collection footprints, acquisition plan and provider metadata | `write_survey_collection_selection()` writes; source selection and Event definition read | Acquisition evidence; not FGDB Collection |
| Source DEM selection and acquisition | GeoPackage file-selection tables plus original external GeoTIFFs and transfer receipts | `write_stream_dem_selection()` and download APIs produce; inspection and mosaic functions read | Sources/provenance; outside governed FGDB feature persistence |
| App Survey Event definition | GeoPackage `settings`, `members`, Stream ID list and `event_links` | `write_survey_acquisition_group()` writes; mask/DEM request functions read | Coordinates shared acquisition inputs and links to Reach Survey Events; not an added hierarchy level |
| Geometry source/piece evidence | GeoPackage line, polygon and cut layers linked to hierarchy IDs | Corridor and Reach-editing functions write/read | Reproducible construction evidence; source COMIDs and piece IDs do not replace FGDB entity IDs |
| Study/Stream/Reach masks | External Byte GeoTIFFs linked to geometry and Event grid | `write_event_masks()` produces; `mask_terrain_mosaic()` consumes | Processing domain, not a governed feature class or observed terrain product |
| Assembled Stream DEM | External Float32 GeoTIFF in international feet on the Event grid | `mosaic_terrain_tiles(template=...)` (same-CRS bilinear resampling) -> `mask_terrain_mosaic()` -> `terrain_to_international_feet()` | Shared Stream terrain consumed by local Hydro Modify; downstream Reach delivery binding remains pending |
| Local DEM execution evidence | Additive `execution` record inside the edition's `edition.rds`; retained backend result metadata for older editions | `launch_terrain_dem_trial()` captures methods, WKT and software; `study_dem_store()` persists; `terrain_dem_provenance_ui()` reads | Bound to the displayed Stream/Event edition; separate from planned operations and not yet portable FGDB delivery metadata |

Study/Stream terrain may support several Reach Events. FGDB's folder requirements
allow explicitly associated shared project assets; they do not require copying
or clipping a raster merely to fit a folder hierarchy. Subsequent Reach/Event
products must retain their own identities, methods and source associations.

## Physical delivery boundary

Transformation plans are another local preparation asset. The Study/Event-bound
JSON revisions under `terrain-transformations` retain the full source/target
reference evidence, operation candidates, resource identities and explicit analyst
choices. `review_terrain_transformations()` discovers candidates;
`study_transform_store()` writes and reopens plans. These are not executed-operation
records or governed FGDB assets. Linking verified execution evidence to DEM
editions remains unfinished; the current same-CRS DEM path is independent of plans.

The existing FGDB delivery contract describes a Reach-Survey-Event folder containing:

- **GeoPackage feature classes and tables:** geometry, attributes, identities and
  relationships governed by the applicable object contracts.
- **External GeoTIFF rasters:** numerical terrain/analysis values with their grid,
  CRS, elevation reference/unit and NoData representation.
- **Linked machine-readable metadata:** owning/context IDs, product role and
  edition, relative asset location, layer or band, integrity and provenance.
- **Related reports and declared shared dependencies.**

This is the accepted structure under FGDB ADR-0025. Exact manifest serialization,
filenames and adapters remain to be bound; the app's internal RDS edition index
is not that manifest. A GeoPackage by itself is not a complete raster-containing
delivery, and a file path is not a durable domain identifier.

Local analysis uses the selected appropriate projected CRS. FGDB's enterprise
contract specifies EPSG:3857 for governed spatial content while retaining native
analysis and vertical-reference evidence. Enterprise publication therefore needs
an explicit qualified boundary transform; the documentation does not imply that
the app's native-grid products are already transformed or accepted.

## Reading function-flow documentation through the data model

For each operation, ask: **Which object is read? Which object is created or
changed? In which feature layer, table or raster does that representation live?
Which identity links it to its parent and inputs?** Preview-only functions have
no durable output. A renamed object retains identity. A processing intermediate
is not promoted to a governed product by being written to disk.

The numbered chapters provide these mappings at the operation boundary. Readers
who need exact working-file resolution can follow `R/study_store.R`,
`R/study_dem_store.R` and the persistence schemas. Internal staging, cache and
revision naming are implementation details, not additions to FGDB's ontology.

## Governing sources

The sibling FGDB repository owns these contracts:

- `dev/schemas/conceptual-data-model.md`: accepted hierarchy and ownership.
- `dev/schemas/feature-catalog.md`: governed objects and exclusions, including
  local source terrain versus the hydro-modified DEM.
- `dev/schemas/kernel-relational-model.md`: proposed identity/edition relations.
- `dev/schemas/platform-type-crosswalk.md`: logical versus physical binding.
- `dev/decisions/adr-0025-folder-deliverables-and-geotiff-terrain.md` and
  `dev/schemas/local-project-folder-requirements.md`: accepted delivery structure
  and unresolved physical binding.

Local context representation is specified in fluvgeo's
`dev/schemas/study-context.md`; app DEM persistence is specified in fgstudio's
`dev/schemas/survey-event-dem.md`. These implementations support the data model
without claiming to complete FGDB conformance or enterprise transport.

Hydro Modify cutlines are local preparation assets linked to the Study, selected
Survey Event, Stream and source DEM edition. `study_hydro_store()` publishes
immutable drawing revisions under the Study's `hydro-modify` directory. Nonempty
drawings use a `cutlines` GeoPackage layer; an internal RDS record retains binding
and revision evidence. Empty revisions retain the deletion state. Applying cuts
publishes a derived `result/hydro-dem.tif` with JSON provenance and an internal
completion index, linked to the source DEM edition and exact drawing revision.
This local preparation result does not complete the governed FGDB hydro DEM or
portable delivery binding.
See [Hydro modification](dev-15-hydro-modify.html) for operation and storage routes.

Regenerable elevation/hillshade COG pyramids live separately under Study-local
`terrain-display`, keyed by source identity and display recipe. Interactive views
reuse these when present and otherwise prepare only temporary viewport rasters;
opening a DEM does not require building a full cache. These caches accelerate
inspection and are not analytical terrain editions or portable FGDB products.
